mappings.note: Kalhana on what a historian must be - impartial, working from inscriptions, temple records and land grants rather than flattery - and how that compares with history written today. CG-SST2's goal statement is exactly 'how historians study the past using different types of sources', but none of its three competencies reaches historiography, so goal level is the honest citation.

Shankaracharya's Advaita teaching of brahman and maya (LO-35, a new religious school) plus marking Badrinath, Puri, Dwarka and Sringeri on a map and reading the choice of the four corners (CG-SST1, since LO-27 covers only climatic regions).

The shift of the imperial capital from Pataliputra to Kannauj and what it did to the subcontinent's politics. A kingdom's strategic and administrative choice, LO-32; LO-33 is rejected because no two rulers' policies are being compared.
Reading Devanagari letters in Harsha's own signature. Working directly from a primary source; goal-level CG-SST2, as no LO covers palaeography.
Xuanzang's route and the Buddhist centres he visited. CG-SST2 for the traveller's account as a historical source, CG-SST1 for tracing passes and deserts on a map, which LO-27 cannot take.

Roman, Persian and Chinese coins at Mamallapuram as evidence of Pallava maritime trade. Archaeological evidence of the period's economy; goal-level CG-SST2, since no LO covers early medieval commerce.
A land grant of forest to Brahmanas aimed at bringing wasteland under the plough and widening the tax base. An administrative measure of a kingdom, LO-32 exactly.

The Bhauma-Kara title 'Paramabhattarika Maharajadhiraja Tribhuvana Mahadevi' and the sovereignty it claims. Royal titulature as an assertion of authority, LO-32; LO-43 is rejected although the holder is a queen, that LO being about disadvantage rather than a woman wielding imperial power.

A letter imagining life in Kannauj during the Pala-Pratihara-Rashtrakuta wars. LO-32 for the struggle for military control of the city, LO-33 because the task explicitly asks for the writer's estimate of the three rulers set against one another.
Advantages and challenges of ruling a core directly while governing the rest through vassals. The structure of authority in a kingdom, LO-32. (This row has an empty answer; see report.)
Huna and Arab invasions compared on aims, methods and impact. LO-33 for the explicit comparison, LO-32 for the military strategies being compared. (Answer breaks off after one sentence; see report.)

A citizen's reaction to Harsha giving away his wealth at Prayaga. The practice is a ruler's deliberate policy of redistribution and legitimacy, LO-32; LO-35 is rejected because no religious idea is being explained, only royal patronage.

Biographies of an Alvar and a Nayanar with sample poems in translation. LO-36 is a direct fit - drawing inferences from bhakti poetry about the social order - rather than LO-35, which would ask why the movement arose.
Writing modern names beside ancient capitals and locating them on a present-day map. Map work on historical places; goal-level CG-SST1, LO-27 being confined to climatic regions.

Matches Rashtrakutas to Manyakheta, Pratiharas to Ujjayini, Cholas to Tanjavur, Harsha to Kanyakubja and Pallavas to Kanchi. Kingdoms and their seats of power, LO-32; CG-SST1 is rejected because the pairing is dynastic, not locational.
How historians mine Harsha's plays - fiction - for governance, social hierarchy, food and dress. A question about method and source type, goal-level CG-SST2.
The five-yearly Prayaga assembly as an occasion for distributing royal wealth to Buddhists, Brahmins and the poor. A ruler's institutional practice, LO-32.

Defines the Tripartite Struggle as the Pala-Pratihara-Rashtrakuta contest for Kannauj. Strategy for military control, LO-32; LO-33 is reserved for items that actually compare the three rulers' policies.
The dvarapandita at Vikramashila who examined candidates before admission. An institution of learning in the period; goal-level CG-SST2, no LO covering education.

Pala prosperity from internal land markets and maritime commerce with Southeast Asia. Economic history of the period, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-32 is rejected because no administrative or military measure is at issue.
Dantidurga overthrowing the Chalukyas to found the Rashtrakuta empire. Military overthrow and dynastic succession, LO-32.
Krishna I commissioning the Kailashanatha at Ellora, cut from a single hillside. Distinctive temple style and construction technique, LO-34 exactly.
Kalhana as author of the Rajatarangini. Identification of a historical source, goal-level CG-SST2.
Defines 'monolithic' as carved from a single rock, with Mamallapuram as the instance. Construction technology of temples, LO-34.
Kashmir Shaivism as the school producing Abhinavagupta. A distinct religious-philosophical development, LO-35; LO-36 is rejected as it concerns bhakti and sufi verse.
Vatapi (Badami), the Chalukya capital, famed for its rock-cut Hindu and Jain cave temples. The discriminating knowledge is the cave-temple complex, so LO-34 rather than LO-32.
Huna descendants absorbed into Indian society through administrative office, Sanskrit and royal titles. Assimilation into the machinery of kingdoms, LO-32.
The original sense of 'Mlechchha' and its drift towards meaning foreigners. Historical terminology from the sources, goal-level CG-SST2.
Why the Arab conquest of Sindh stayed contained - resistance by Indian rulers confined it to the northwest. Military strategy and its limits, LO-32.
The Chachnama as a Persian rendering of an older Arabic account of the Sindh conquest. A question about the nature and transmission of a source, goal-level CG-SST2.
The Puranas absorbing local deities and myths into the Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions. The formation of religious traditions, LO-35; LO-36 is rejected as it is specific to bhakti and sufi poetry.

A 9th-century merchant guild sponsoring an irrigation tank for prestige. Guild patronage in the period's economy and society, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-31 is rejected because the point is social standing, not water conservation.
Names 600-1200 CE the Early Medieval period. Periodisation, a historian's category; goal-level CG-SST2.
Harsha's accession at Kannauj in 606 CE. Dynastic fact about a kingdom's rule, LO-32, which is where this frame houses dynastic history; CG-SST2 is kept for source and method items.
Sthaneshvara as the Pushyabhuti capital before Kannauj. Seat of a kingdom, LO-32, matching the capital-shift item.
Banabhatta as author of the Harshacharita and Kadambari. Identification of a court source, goal-level CG-SST2 rather than LO-32, since the question is about the text, not the reign.
Xuanzang's Indian journey of 630-644 CE. A foreign traveller's record as a source, goal-level CG-SST2.

Gopala chosen in 750 CE to restore order in Bengal, founding the Pala line. The making of royal authority, LO-32; the 'chosen by the people' detail does not reach LO-41, which is the modern legislative assembly.
Dharmapala founding Vikramashila on the Ganga. Royal foundation and patronage, LO-32; the discriminator in the options is which ruler and which university, not the Buddhism taught there.
Nagabhata I founding the Gurjara-Pratihara line, noted for holding off Arab invasions. Dynastic founding and military role, LO-32.
King Bhoja's northern empire and his title Adi Varaha, with the Madurai claim as the false statement. Kingdom and titulature, LO-32. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)

Al-Masudi's praise of a Rashtrakuta ruler's armies and his protection of mosques. CG-SST2 for reading a foreign traveller's testimony, LO-32 for the ruler's military strength and policy towards his subjects.

How an occupational group hardens into a jati through endogamy, custom and inheritance of trade. Social history of the period; goal-level CG-SST2, as C-SST3.1's equality outcomes are about the Constitution, not medieval society.
Sulaiman calling a Pratihara ruler a foe of the Muslim faith, and why. CG-SST2 for interrogating a traveller's viewpoint, LO-32 for the cavalry and resistance that provoked it.
Completing a table of Sanskrit-Arabic cognates - sandal, tanbul, kafur, filfil. Evidence of exchange through trade and translation, goal-level CG-SST2.

Why land-grant inscriptions praise the ruler in Sanskrit but record the operative terms in the local language. LO-32 for the grant as an administrative instrument, CG-SST2 for reading the inscription as a source.
Sorts Narasimhavarman I's real achievements - the Mamalla title, the defeat of Pulakeshin II, the Sri Lanka expedition - from a false capital shift. Military and dynastic record, LO-32.
The Pandyas at Madurai and their patronage of a Tamil Mahabharata. Kingdom, capital and court patronage, LO-32.
Vijayalaya laying the foundation of the revived Chola power at Tanjavur. Dynastic re-founding, LO-32.

The Uttaramerur inscriptions recording how Chola village sabha members were selected. Local administration under a kingdom, LO-32; LO-41 is rejected outright, being the election process for a modern State legislative assembly.
The Kayasthas, scribes and clerks, consolidating into a jati by the 10th century. Social history, goal-level CG-SST2, same reasoning as the jati-formation item.

Tests the false claim that no woman ruled, against Tribhuvana Mahadevi and women's economic and religious patronage. LO-43 is the only outcome in this frame addressing women's position; cited although the item rebuts rather than illustrates disadvantage, which is the gap worth noting.

The Bhakti movement in the south under the Alvars and Nayanars, offering direct devotion across social barriers. LO-35 for the emergence of the movement; LO-36 is reserved for items that work from the poetry itself.
Brahmagupta's rules for zero and negative numbers. History of science in the period; goal-level CG-SST2, no LO covering intellectual achievement.
Hunas assimilating through military service, Sanskrit and Gupta-style titles and coin symbols. Absorption into the apparatus of kingship, LO-32.
Why Muhammad bin Qasim attacked Sindh - sent by the governor of Iraq to conquer and defeat Dahar. Military strategy, LO-32.

Indian rulers such as Nagabhata I and Lalitaditya resisting the Arabs, sometimes in alliance. Military strategy and coalition, LO-32; LO-33 is rejected because no comparison of their policies is drawn.
Arab rule in Sindh shifting to allow Hindus and Buddhists to rebuild and worship. A change in a ruling power's policy towards its subjects, LO-32.
Indian mathematics and astronomy reaching Europe through Arab translation and the decimal system. Transmission of knowledge across the period; goal-level CG-SST2.
